query: Which monitoring diagnostics and interim checks should be pre-specified to trigger adaptive responses to low compliance or low passive-data consent?

response.query: Which monitoring diagnostics and interim checks should be pre-specified to trigger adaptive responses to low compliance or low passive-data consent?
response.answer: Monitoring diagnostics should include compliance audits and passive-data consent checks. Low compliance triggers corrective actions, while low consent prompts consent re-evaluation. Adaptive responses depend on predefined thresholds for these checks.

results.title: Uniform Data System 2025 MANUAL
results.content: The Uniform Data System (UDS) provides consistent information about health centers including patient characteristics, services provided, clinical processes. • If the health center brings services into its approved scope of project at any time during the calendar year, the health center must include data for those services in its UDS Report for the full calendar year. • If the health center brings service delivery sites into its approved scope of project during the calendar year, the health center must include data for the new service delivery sites in its UDS Report for the period beginning on the date of the scope change or the New Access Point (NAP) site implementation date. • UDS state and national summary tables and Health Center Program awardee and look-alike data profiles will be available in the  HRSA Data Warehouse  in August 2026. Services provided: Availability and use of care that a patient may receive from the health center.

results.title: A Pragmatic CDO's Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 8 — ...
results.content: # **A Pragmatic CDO’s Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 8 — Healthcare Data Quality Playbook: Codes, Encounters, Consent, Outcomes**. ## Healthcare quality is measured in lives and compliance. We manage ICD/CPT/LOINC/SNOMED versioning, encounter stitching, provider/payer identity, claims CDC, and PHI masking side-effects. NHS DQMI and FHIR-based quality reporting (eCQMs, Bulk FHIR) provide measurement and exchange frameworks. * **Clinical Code Stewardship**: Maintain rigorous version control for medical code systems (ICD-10, CPT, LOINC, SNOMED CT, RxNorm, UCUM). **Data contracts** must specify code system and version, validate codes against effective dates, and enforce standard units (UCUM) [1], [2]. Automated checks catch retired or unknown codes and inconsistent units to prevent downstream analytics errors. * **ADT & FHIR Interface Contracts**: Define **Admit-Discharge-Transfer (ADT)** and **FHIR API** data contracts with required fields, timeliness SLAs, and format constraints. ## Written by Adnan Masood, PhD. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.

results.content: See *Data.CMS.gov,* Medicare Shared Savings Program, Accountable Care Organizations, Public Use File (by performance year, for PY 2025), available at *https://data.cms.gov/​medicare-shared-savings-program/​accountable-care-organizations.*. Message to the Quality Payment Program listserv on January 4, 2025, entitled “The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is Soliciting Stakeholder Recommendations for Potential Consideration of New Specialty Measure Sets and/or Revisions to the Existing Specialty Measure Sets for the 2026 Performance Year of the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS).”. Section 101(b) of the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015 (MACRA) sunset the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals, set forth at section 1848(o) of the Act. As discussed previously, section 1848(o)(2) of the Act has been incorporated into the MIPS Promoting Interoperability performance category's requirements via section 1848(q)(2)(B)(iv) of the Act. See CY 2017 Quality Payment Program final rule (81 FR 77018 and 77019) for more information regarding the sunsetting of the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals.
